status: REAL RESULT — rank #8 by E-distance (gate-passing). Interpreted as a DE-PRIORITIZED brake (weak effect + over-proliferation flag), but tractability UPGRADED: a clinical-stage DGKa inhibitor now exists.
modality_context: KO (Shifrut/Marson primary human CD8 T-cell CRISPR-KO); concordance rule: concordant = protective_lof

real_result.interpretation: Statistically significant but SMALL causal footprint (E=0.61 — ~7x below the RASA2/CBLB brake tier and the weakest gate-passing hit). Highest viability_ratio in the panel (2.30) = KO drives OVER-proliferation, so its signature is a fitness/expansion effect more than a clean effector-program shift. Gate-passing but low-priority.

ensembl_expected: ENSG00000065357 (literature; unverified — OT unavailable this run to confirm)

identifiers.chembl_target_note: SINGLE PROTEIN target 'Diacylglycerol kinase alpha' (P23743; PDB 1TUZ, 6IIE). ChEMBL also lists PROTEIN FAMILY target CHEMBL4630754 (DGKalpha/zeta) — the dual-isozyme node most IO drug-discovery programs pursue (DGKa and DGKz redundantly brake TCR-DAG signaling).

io_rationale: DGKa phosphorylates diacylglycerol (DAG) to phosphatidic acid, TERMINATING DAG-driven RasGRP/PKC signaling downstream of the TCR — a metabolic BRAKE on T-cell activation. KO/inhibition sustains DAG signaling and enhances effector function and anti-tumor immunity (well-established IO rationale; DGKa/z double-KO is a strong CAR-T potency enhancer). Direction here is enhancement-consistent, but the effect size in this screen is weak and the readout is proliferative.

tractability.evidence: ChEMBL target CHEMBL4105787 (PDB 1TUZ, 6IIE) + Pharos listing. Historically drugged only by tool compounds (R59022, R59949, ritanserin-class), but a purpose-built oral DGKa inhibitor has now reached the clinic (see known_drugs / active_trials).

genetic_evidence.anchor_disease: none with a usable common-variant direction of effect
genetic_evidence.rationale: No genome-wide-significant immune disease-risk variant with an interpretable LoF direction was established for DGKA; carried as any_gwas=false / no_direction in the concordance funnel. Mechanistic direction (brake) is textbook, but the human-genetics directional axis is absent (pending OT).

known_drugs.action_types: INHIBITOR (tool compounds historically; oral clinical inhibitor now in trials)
examples: BAY 2862789 — Bayer oral DGKa inhibitor (clinical; see active_trials)
ritanserin / R59022 / R59949 — historical DGKa tool inhibitors (preclinical, non-selective)
known_drugs.note: 0 mechanisms in ChEMBL v34 (the clinical DGKa inhibitor post-dates the release); the clinical program was confirmed live via ClinicalTrials.gov.

active_trials.note: REAL clinical validation of DGKa as a druggable IO target — a completed first-in-human Phase 1 (Bayer). Upgrades DGKA from 'preclinical IO' to clinical-stage tractability. Does NOT change its de-prioritization here, which rests on the weak screen effect + over-proliferation flag.

essentiality.note: Not pan-essential; isozyme redundancy with DGKz (dual inhibition is the usual strategy). Immune/lipid-signaling restricted.

safety_flags: In-screen viability_ratio 2.30 (highest in panel) — KO drives over-proliferation; monitor for uncontrolled expansion / exhaustion-independent growth in a cell product.
DAG signaling is broad — on-target inhibition could carry pleiotropic (e.g., platelet, neuronal) effects; the clinical Phase 1 will inform the human safety profile.
call: DE-PRIORITIZE as a lead (weakest gate-passing effect + over-proliferation), but flag as the most CLINICALLY DE-RISKED of the de-prioritized tier — a completed Phase 1 DGKa inhibitor exists. Better pursued as combination/CAR-T-enhancer (with DGKz) than as a standalone KO hero here.
